newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sugar faces A$50 mln-plus damage.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sugar faces A$50 mln-plus damage.

text.p: Cyclone damage to the sugar industry in the north of the Australian state of Queensland would run to tens of millions of Australian dollars, Ian Ballantyne, general manager, CANEGROWERS, said in a statement.
The 2,400 canegrowers north of Townsville were still counting the cost of damage left by cyclone Justin but sugar industry losses could easily exceed A$50 million, he said.

Annual sugar production in North Queensland was worth A$500 million-A$600 million a year and even a 10 percent reduction in yield would trim more than A$50 million from the value of the crop, he said.

There would be additional substantial costs for repairing roads, buildings, paddocks and other industry infrastructure as well as the reduced multiplier effect of sugar earnings throughout the community, he said.
Winds of up to 130 km an hour flattened most of the cane in the region between Ingham and Mossman, which produces more than one-third of Queensland's sugarcane, he said.

Growers' incomes would be slashed as a result of reduced sugar content and higher harvesting and replanting costs, while sugar millers faced higher processing costs because of increased dirt and other extraneous matter in the cane supply, he said.
If the commercial cane sugar (CCS) level of the entire North Queensland cane crop were reduced by just one unit, A$40 million would be wiped off the season's income, he said.

Equally serious was the potential for further heavy financial losses in the Herbert River district where much of the near record 5.3 million tonne crop had been flattened by winds and was now under more than half a metre of water, he said.
Growers faced another problem with an expected shortage of straight cane for planting.
The full extent of flood damage would not be known for some time, he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
